candidates.name: OGC API - Features - Part 5 / OGC API - Common - Part 3: Schemas
verified_facts: Approved OGC implementation standard published 30 April 2026.
Defines logical collection schemas plus /schema, /queryables and /sortables resources.
Queryables describe property names, types and constraints usable in filter expressions; actual-domain and valid-domain profiles are distinct.
semantic_limits: Schema and queryable discovery describe metadata structure and filterability; they do not identify the contributing EA LiDAR survey or validate elevation values.

candidates.name: OGC API - Records - Part 1: Core
verified_facts: Approved OGC implementation standard published 2 May 2025.
Defines catalog records for discovering resources and supports spatial/temporal search.
Filtering can combine CQL2 with bbox, datetime and additional record predicates; all specified predicates must evaluate true for inclusion.
semantic_limits: A matching catalog record is discovery evidence only; it is not automatically the exact composite survey feature or a terrain sample.

candidates.name: OGC Features and Geometries JSON - Part 1: Core
verified_facts: Approved OGC implementation standard published 30 April 2026.
Extends GeoJSON with explicit temporal information and coordinate reference systems beyond WGS 84.
Can declare feature types and feature schemas; feature schemas can conform to OGC API Features Part 5 Schemas.
semantic_limits: JSON-FG encoding can preserve CRS/time/schema semantics but does not increase source accuracy or prove EA survey lineage.

candidates.name: Metadata: Understanding information provided with each DSP dataset
verified_facts: DSP states every published dataset is accompanied by a metadata record.
Metadata attributes are intended to describe the data, intended use and known limitations.
semantic_limits: Dataset-level metadata provides context and limitations; it is not a parcel elevation observation or a survey-feature match.

candidates.name: Survey Data Catalogue - where to view and download metadata for all LiDAR products
verified_facts: EA directs users to the LIDAR Capture Programme for product metadata and coverage maps.
EA states that where no data is listed, that location has not been surveyed by the programme.
semantic_limits: Metadata/coverage availability is discovery evidence and must not be promoted to an exact contributing-survey identity without feature-level matching.
